plan.title: P1-U3: no-agent fixture test, steps 4 and 6 (missing packages, old layout) (ovpr-p1-u3)

narratives.Description: OVPR fix plan unit P1-U3 (story id ovpr-p1-u3), spec units/P1-U3-no-agent-fixture-test.md. A CI test that installs the packed packages into a throwaway repo and runs the registered hook commands exactly as a host would, with no agent. This unit builds the harness and steps 4 (delete node_modules, every host blocks with project install text) and 6 (old-layout fixtures get the old-repo message). Steps 1, 2, 3 and 5 are registered as skip; P3-U1b and P4-U1 add them.
narratives.Overview:
Acceptance criteria (spec P1-U3):
1. The CLI runs with no agent and prints one line per step 1–6. Steps 1, 2, 3 and 5 report `skip`. Steps 4 and 6 report `pass` on a tip that includes P1-U1 and P1-U2.
2. Step 4 fails if any host's `tool.before` does not block after `node_modules` is deleted, or if the text names `npm i -g` or `install --repair`.
3. Step 4's sanity check fails if a hook blocks `echo hi` while the packages are installed.
4. Step 6 fails if any old-layout fixture on any host is not blocked, or lacks the old-repo message. 6f fails if a new-layout repo gets the old-repo message.
5. A later ticket adds a step by adding one `FixtureStep` object and its fixture builder. No other step changes.
6. The CI job finishes within its 12-minute timeout and reports its duration.
narratives.ImplementationPlan:
1. Harness packages/core/src/release-e2e/ovpr-lifecycle-fixture.ts + ovpr-lifecycle-fixture-cli.ts: ordered named steps (1-bump, 2-install, 3-refresh, 4-missing-packages, 5-upgrade-commit, 6-old-layout) over one shared context; each step builds its own fixture dir and can run alone (--step N); 1/2/3/5 skip ('added by P3-U1b' / 'added by P4-U1'); one line per step, non-zero exit on any fail. Lift the shared pack/install helpers from the greenfield harness into release-e2e/packed-consumer.ts; greenfield behaviour unchanged.
2. runRegisteredHook(fixtureDir, host, event, payload): read the deposited host config, take the command for the event, run it via sh -c in the fixture dir with the JSON payload on stdin.
3. expectBlocked(host, result, textMatchers): the P1-U1 block table.
4. Step 4 (missing packages) and step 6 (old layout, fixtures 6a-6f, static files only, v0.126.2 Grok wrapper bytes from the tag under packages/core/src/release-e2e/fixtures/pre-ovpr/).
5. CI: job ovpr-fixture in .github/workflows/ci.yml (D-020; not a new workflow file), artifact-only changes gating like the other ci.yml jobs, timeout-minutes 12, NOT in merge-gate's needs (advisory through Phase 4). Record the measured duration in the PR.
6. Unit test ovpr-lifecycle-fixture.test.ts (fast, no packing).
7. Changelog fragment changelog.d/6614-ovpr-lifecycle-fixture.md (never CHANGELOG.md).
narratives.Constraint:
Must not do:
- No agent, no LLM, no network beyond this repo's own pnpm install. Step 6 must not download any old Directive version.
- Do not run old Directive code: the old Grok wrapper is a host-config stand-in that only calls the new deft-hook.
- Do not change the greenfield smoke's behaviour; only move shared helpers.
- Do not assert exact message wording beyond the key phrases (P4-U3a will reword).
- Do not add the job to merge-gate's needs before the Phase 4 exit (D-020). Never change repository settings (D-007).
- OVPR change gate: do not edit docs/installer-refactor-ovpr/ or ship behaviour that departs from the written OVPR design; stop and hand back a change proposal if needed.
narratives.Dependencies: Depends on ovpr-p1-u1 (step 4 asserts its block forms) and ovpr-p1-u2 (step 6 asserts its message). Blocks P3-U1b (steps 1-3) and P4-U1 (step 5). Windows leg is #6621 (separate).
narratives.DesignCritique: design-critique: not warranted, because the OVPR fix plan and this unit spec already decide the design (polfer decisions D-001, D-008)
narratives.UserStory: As a Directive maintainer, I want a CI test that installs the packed packages into a throwaway repo and runs the registered hook commands with no agent, so that CI fails when a hook stops blocking after node_modules is deleted or in an old-layout repo.

items.title: The CLI runs with no agent and prints one line per step 1–6. Steps 1, 2, 3 and 5 report `skip`. Steps 4 and 6 report `pass` on a tip that includes P1-U1 and P1-U2.

narrative.Acceptance: Given a build on a tip with P1-U1 and P1-U2, when node packages/core/dist/release-e2e/ovpr-lifecycle-fixture-cli.js runs, then it prints six step lines, 1/2/3/5 skip and 4/6 pass.

items.title: Step 4 fails if any host's `tool.before` does not block after `node_modules` is deleted, or if the text names `npm i -g` or `install --repair`.

narrative.Acceptance: Given node_modules deleted, when tool.before runs on each host, then step 4 passes only if every host blocks with npm install or pnpm install text and none names npm i -g or install --repair.

items.title: Step 4's sanity check fails if a hook blocks `echo hi` while the packages are installed.

narrative.Acceptance: Given an installed fixture, when tool.before runs echo hi on each host, then no host blocks, or step 4 fails.

items.title: Step 6 fails if any old-layout fixture on any host is not blocked, or lacks the old-repo message. 6f fails if a new-layout repo gets the old-repo message.

narrative.Acceptance: Given fixtures 6a-6e, when tool.before runs on each host, then each blocks with text containing pre-OVPR, directive upgrade and npm i -g @deftai/directive@0.126.2; given 6f, then the old-repo message does not appear.

items.title: A later ticket adds a step by adding one `FixtureStep` object and its fixture builder. No other step changes.

narrative.Acceptance: Given the harness, then each step is one FixtureStep object in an ordered registry with its own fixture builder, and the unit test checks the registry order and ids.

items.title: The CI job finishes within its 12-minute timeout and reports its duration.

narrative.Acceptance: Given the ovpr-fixture job in .github/workflows/ci.yml on the PR, then it finishes within timeout-minutes 12 and the PR records its duration.

sentences: test(ovpr): no-agent fixture test for the pin lifecycle (bump, install, refresh, missing packages, upgrade commit, old layout)
Problem Directive's install and hook behaviour is proven mostly by unit tests that call functions in-process.
Nothing in CI installs the packed packages into a throwaway repo, runs the registered hook commands the way an AI host does, and checks the result.
So two failures shipped unnoticed: hooks fail open when `node_modules` is missing (#6201), and old-layout repos lose checking (#5960).
The fix needs a test that runs with no agent, so it also proves the design works in a plain CI or Dependabot flow.
Evidence (origin/master `def527f5e`): - #6170 added one in-process unit test, `packages/runtime/src/self-complete.test.ts:285` ("AC14.10 / HT-17").
It calls `runSetup` and `maybeSelfCompleteSetup` directly.
No packing, no real install, no hook command.
It is the logic oracle for later steps 1–3, not a harness to extend.
A packed-consumer harness already exists: `packages/core/src/release-e2e/greenfield-python-free-smoke.ts:238` (`rehearseGreenfieldPythonFreeSmoke`).

It uses `alignNpmPackageVersions` and `packOvprTarballs` (`npm-ops.ts:102`, `:166`), installs the packed tarballs globally (`:336-338`), installs the exact runtime pin into a temp consumer (`:379`), and runs `install --repair --yes` (`:446`).
Its workflow, `.github/workflows/greenfield-python-free-smoke.yml`, hosts no required check.
Today the `.mjs` outer's missing-pin path exits 1 on every host except Grok (`packages/core/src/init-deposit/host-hook-outer.ts:324-333`).
Exit 1 does not block on Claude or Codex (#6201).
What the design says - AC14.3, AC9.12, AC9.4: a missing pin fails closed, with project install guidance.
§A9 / AC10.2: an old layout gets a "run `directive upgrade`" message.
Old code never runs.
AC14.10: a pin-only bump plus the PM install; the first eligible hook completes wiring (steps 1–3, added later).
Decision `xbrief/decisions/2026-11-10-close-5947-5948-…decision.json`: pin-only bumps are legal.
D-013: when no runtime is installed, the hook fails closed and a person runs the project install.
D-018: a missing package blocks only before a tool runs.
Step 4 tests `tool.before` only.
D-020: the job lives in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`.
It is advisory through Phase 4.
At the Phase 4 exit, a reviewed `ci.yml` PR adds it to the `merge-gate` job (`Merge gate (task check)`, `ci.yml:558-559`).
No repository setting changes (D-007).
The Windows leg (AC15.1) is #6621.
Expected 1.

Harness `packages/core/src/release-e2e/ovpr-lifecycle-fixture.ts` and `ovpr-lifecycle-fixture-cli.ts`, built as an ordered list of named steps (`1-bump`, `2-install`, `3-refresh`, `4-missing-packages`, `5-upgrade-commit`, `6-old-layout`) over one shared context, so a later ticket adds a step without touching the others.
Setup once: align versions, pack, and `npm install -g` the packed launcher and runtime into a temp prefix.
Lift the shared helpers out of the greenfield harness into `release-e2e/packed-consumer.ts`.
Greenfield's behaviour does not change.
Each step builds its own fixture directory, so a step can run alone (`--step 4`).
Steps 1, 2, 3 and 5 are registered as `skip` ("added by P3-U1b" / "added by P4-U1").
The runner prints one line per step and exits non-zero on any `fail`.
Hook runner `runRegisteredHook(fixtureDir, host, event, payload)`.

It reads the host config Directive deposited (`.claude/settings.json`, `.codex/hooks.json`, `.cursor/hooks.json`, `.grok/hooks/deft.json`), takes the command for that event, and runs it through `sh -c` in the fixture directory with the JSON payload on stdin.
The step fails if a host config or its `tool.before` entry is missing.

Block helper `expectBlocked(host, result, textMatchers)`: Claude and Codex exit 2 with matching stderr; Cursor exits 0 with exactly one object with `permission: "deny"` (exit 2 is also accepted); Grok exits 0 with exactly one object with `decision: "deny"`.
Same table as P1-U1 (#6201).
Step 4, missing packages. Make an installed fixture.
Sanity check first: on each host, `tool.before` for `echo hi` does not block.
Then delete `node_modules` and run `tool.before` on each host.
Expect a block whose text contains `npm install` or `pnpm install`, and does not contain `npm i -g` or `install --repair`.
Step 6, old layout. No install and no network.

Static fixtures only; no 0.126 package is downloaded: - 6a exact `"@deftai/directive": "0.126.2"` + `.deft/core/VERSION`; - 6b `"^0.126.2"` + `.deft/core/VERSION`; - 6c no root dependency, nested `tools/deft-cli/package.json` `"^0.126.1"`, root `.deft/core/package.json` with `deftConsumerDeposit: true`; - 6d `"^0.126.2"`, no `.deft/core`, `.githooks/_deft-run.sh` present (fresh-clone shape); - 6e like 6b, but the Claude config registers `deft hook:dispatch --host claude --event tool.before`.
Fixtures 6a–6d carry the four v0.126.2 host configs.
The Grok wrapper bytes come from tag v0.126.2 (not master) and are stored under `packages/core/src/release-e2e/fixtures/pre-ovpr/`.
Expect a block on every host, with text containing `pre-OVPR`, `directive upgrade` and `npm i -g @deftai/directive@0.126.2`.
6f negative control: a new-layout installed fixture whose Claude config still has a bare `deft-hook` entry does not get the old-repo message.
CI. Job `ovpr-fixture` in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (D-020; not a new workflow file).

Record the measured duration in the PR (target under 5 minutes; unverified until the first run).
Unit test `ovpr-lifecycle-fixture.test.ts`: step order and ids, `skip` for 1/2/3/5, the `expectBlocked` table against canned results, config parsing per host.
Fast, no packing.
